facts.claim: At capacity; pre-qualification closed. Pre-qualifications already on the waitlist are processed first come, first served. Financing up to 100% of project cost to $50,000, repaid on the property tax bill over the lesser of 20 years or the upgrades' useful life. Interest rate currently 1.62%, variable up to but not over 3%. Minimum project $3,000.
Residential CEIP is offered in Calgary, Edmonton, Lethbridge, St. Albert (among others). Red Deer and Wood Buffalo (Fort McMurray) are NOT on the residential list.

Edmonton residential CEIP: financing of $3,000 to $50,000, up to 100% of cost, fixed 6.00% (current tranche), term up to 20 years or the upgrades' useful life, repaid on property tax, penalty-free early payoff. At least three upgrades are required (unless fewer reach net zero or the property took part before). Not eligible in Edmonton: air conditioners, high-efficiency gas furnaces (unless combined with a heat pump), high-efficiency storage water heaters. The program is nearing capacity and new pre-qualifications go on a waitlist, first come, first served. Initial $20 million supports roughly 300 residential projects; intake pauses after 150 pre-qualifications. City FAQ: 'Currently, there are no available rebates' from the City of Edmonton.
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-03 (edmonton.ca loaded). 2026-10-09: edmonton.ca returned 502, so not re-read; amounts rest on the 2026-10-03 read.

facts.claim: EPCOR page: $50 prepaid Mastercard for enrolling (one per household) plus $25 per season for participating; EPCOR distribution area, central air conditioning, compatible smart thermostat you already own (ecobee, Honeywell Home, Google Nest); select Edmonton neighbourhoods; setpoint changed up to 3°C for up to four hours; opt out any time. Phase 2: EV Enabled Rebate 50% up to $6,000 per stall ($90,000 max); EV Charger Rebate 50% up to $1,000 single-port / $2,000 dual-port ($10,000 max), only with EV Enabled Rebate; $100,000 per property. Phase 2 applications closed November 18, 2025; cohort notified January 2026. Not for detached houses.

facts.claim: Electrical permit required for new wiring. Homeowner permit $116.50 ($112 + 4% fee). Homeowners are not permitted to install electrical wiring for EV charging, alter the main service, or do load calculations; a licensed electrician must. Apartment-style condos need a licensed contractor; row-house units need condo board authorization and a load calculation.

Get a certified electrician and a load calculation first. Level 2 chargers start at $499 CAD excluding installation; full charge 6-14 h (battery EV). Options if service is short: smaller charger (30 A instead of 50 A; average driver needs under 3 h a night) or EV energy management system (approx. $1,200). No ENMAX home charger rebate listed.

Funds chargers in public places, on-street, multi-unit residential buildings, workplaces and fleets (50% of costs); not individual homeowners. Owner/operator streams closed for applications. Program runs to March 31, 2027.

Federal incentive toward buying or leasing an eligible electric vehicle (transactions from February 16, 2026) until March 31, 2031 or until funds run out (about $1.92 billion left on October 1, 2026). It is for vehicles, not home chargers.
